readings.section: CKVA Day 1: Introduction to Art of the Middle Ages in Europe - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Explore and summarize the defining features of art in the European Middle Ages.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 1: Introduction to Art of the Middle Ages in Europe (Middle Ages in Europe)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Summarize defining features and themes of art of the European Middle Ages.

ckva.lesson: Introduction to Art of the Middle Ages in Europe

readings.section: CKVA Day 2: The Madonna and Child in Medieval Art - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Learn about the Madonna as a main subject in medieval artwork. Artwork: Madonna and Child on a Curved Throne.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 2: The Madonna and Child in Medieval Art (Middle Ages in Europe)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Analyze the style and symbolism of the Madonna in medieval artwork.

ckva.lesson: The Madonna and Child in Medieval Art

readings.section: CKVA Day 3: Illuminated Manuscripts - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Create an original two-page illuminated manuscript based on your initials. Artwork: Chi Rho Page from the Book of Kells. Supplies: markers or colored pencils (including gold), white paper (2 sheets), eraser, black ink pen (optional).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 3: Illuminated Manuscripts (Middle Ages in Europe)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Describe the features and purposes of illuminated manuscripts.

readings.section: CKVA Day 4: Tapestries - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Learn how medieval tapestries were designed and used, then build a cardboard loom. Artwork: The Unicorn in Captivity (Tapestry). Supplies: drawing paper, cardboard 8 x 12 in, ruler, scissors, tape, yarn (about 10 ft).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 4: Tapestries (Middle Ages in Europe)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Identify the artistic, decorative and practical purposes of medieval tapestries.

readings.section: CKVA Day 5: Creating Art of the Middle Ages - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Review medieval art and create artwork that represents the Middle Ages. Supplies: sketch paper, drawing paper, pencil and eraser, markers, colored pencils or watercolors.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 5: Creating Art of the Middle Ages (Middle Ages in Europe)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Represent the characteristics of medieval art in an original artwork.

ckva.lesson: Creating Art of the Middle Ages

readings.section: CKVA Day 6: Gothic Architecture (day 1 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Learn the elements of Gothic architecture. Artwork: Notre Dame Cathedral. Supplies: writing paper, pencil.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 6: Gothic Architecture (day 1 of 2) (Middle Ages in Europe)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Describe the features of Gothic architecture and explain their purpose.

readings.section: CKVA Day 7: Gothic Architecture (day 2 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Learn about gargoyles and sculpt your own gargoyle from clay. Supplies: air-dry clay, sculpting tools (plastic knife, toothpicks), small bowl of water, washable work surface.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 7: Gothic Architecture (day 2 of 2) (Middle Ages in Europe)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Describe the features of Gothic architecture and explain their purpose.

readings.section: CKVA Day 8: Unit 1 Assessment - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Make a rose window to show what you learned in Unit 1. Supplies: black construction paper, white chalk, scissors, colored tissue paper or cellophane, glue stick.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 8: Unit 1 Assessment (Middle Ages in Europe)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Show understanding of medieval art through a performance task.

readings.section: CKVA Day 9: Characteristics of Islamic Art - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Match pictures to the element of Islamic art they show.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 9: Characteristics of Islamic Art (Islamic Art and Architecture)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Recognize elements of religious and secular Islamic art.

readings.section: CKVA Day 10: Patterns and Illumination (day 1 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Create artwork from repeating geometric patterns. Artwork: Illumination of the Qur'an. Supplies: graph paper, ruler, pencil and eraser, colored pencils or markers.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 10: Patterns and Illumination (day 1 of 2) (Islamic Art and Architecture)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Analyze how and why geometric patterns were used in Islamic art.

readings.section: CKVA Day 11: Patterns and Illumination (day 2 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Complete your repeating geometric pattern artwork. Supplies: graph paper, ruler, colored pencils or markers.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 11: Patterns and Illumination (day 2 of 2) (Islamic Art and Architecture)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Analyze how and why geometric patterns were used in Islamic art.

readings.section: CKVA Day 12: Intersection of Art and Architecture (day 1 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Identify elements of Islamic architecture. Artwork: Court of the Lions, Dome of the Rock.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 12: Intersection of Art and Architecture (day 1 of 2) (Islamic Art and Architecture)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Identify the structural and decorative features of Islamic architecture.

readings.section: CKVA Day 13: Intersection of Art and Architecture (day 2 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Design architectural plans for an Islamic building or monument. Artwork: Taj Mahal. Supplies: sketch paper (2 sheets), pencil and eraser, ruler.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 13: Intersection of Art and Architecture (day 2 of 2) (Islamic Art and Architecture)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Identify the structural and decorative features of Islamic architecture.

readings.section: CKVA Day 14: Unit 2 Assessment - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Answer questions about the Taj Mahal to review Unit 2. Artwork: Taj Mahal. Supplies: pencil.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 14: Unit 2 Assessment (Islamic Art and Architecture)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Show understanding of Islamic art and architecture.

readings.section: CKVA Day 15: Introduction to Art of Africa - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Learn that African art has practical and traditional purposes.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 15: Introduction to Art of Africa (The Art of Africa)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Compare the purposes and functions of African art with art of other cultures.

readings.section: CKVA Day 16: Portraying Leaders (day 1 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Examine sculpted portrait heads that represent African leaders. Artwork: Benin Bronze Head, Portrait Head of an Ife King.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 16: Portraying Leaders (day 1 of 2) (The Art of Africa)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Analyze how leaders are portrayed in traditional African art.

readings.section: CKVA Day 17: Portraying Leaders (day 2 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Create a royal self-portrait that communicates a personal message. Supplies: drawing paper, pencil and eraser, markers, colored pencils or watercolors.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 17: Portraying Leaders (day 2 of 2) (The Art of Africa)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Analyze how leaders are portrayed in traditional African art.

readings.section: CKVA Day 18: Masks: Carvings and Sculptures (day 1 of 2) - view the artwork online
readings.note: Learn about African carvings, masks and headdresses. Artwork: Face Mask, Bamana Antelope Headdress of Mali.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 18: Masks: Carvings and Sculptures (day 1 of 2) (The Art of Africa)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Analyze the form and function of traditional African masks and headdresses.

readings.section: CKVA Day 19: Masks: Carvings and Sculptures (day 2 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Create an animal mask inspired by traditional African art. Supplies: construction paper, glue, clear tape, scissors, craft stick, natural decorations (feathers, leaves, seeds).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 19: Masks: Carvings and Sculptures (day 2 of 2) (The Art of Africa)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Analyze the form and function of traditional African masks and headdresses.

readings.section: CKVA Day 20: Contemporary and Ancient Connections - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Create a collage inspired by contemporary African collage artists. Supplies: heavy drawing paper, magazines, scissors, glue, paints or markers (optional).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 20: Contemporary and Ancient Connections (The Art of Africa)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Compare contemporary African art with traditional African art.

readings.section: CKVA Day 21: Unit 3 Assessment - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Create a painting that shows characteristics of African art. Supplies: canvas panel or heavy paper, acrylic paints, brushes and palette, cup of water, paper towels.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 21: Unit 3 Assessment (The Art of Africa)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Show understanding of the art of Africa.

readings.section: CKVA Day 22: Introduction to Art of China - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Read and answer questions about the Chinese invention of silk and paper.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 22: Introduction to Art of China (The Art of China)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Identify Chinese artistic inventions and the art forms Chinese artists excelled in.

readings.section: CKVA Day 23: Calligraphy - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Practice writing Chinese calligraphy. Artwork: Calligraphy. Supplies: heavy drawing or watercolor paper, black calligraphy pen, marker, or pointed brush with black paint.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 23: Calligraphy (The Art of China)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Identify the purpose and techniques of traditional Chinese calligraphy.

readings.section: CKVA Day 24: Landscapes (day 1 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Reflect on the artistic qualities of a silk scroll painting. Artwork: Lonely Retreat Overlooking a Misty Valley (Silk Scroll).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 24: Landscapes (day 1 of 2) (The Art of China)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Describe how traditional Chinese artists painted landscapes on scrolls.

readings.section: CKVA Day 25: Landscapes (day 2 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Paint a landscape inspired by traditional Chinese art. Supplies: watercolor paper, watercolor paints, brushes, cup of water, paper towels.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 25: Landscapes (day 2 of 2) (The Art of China)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Describe how traditional Chinese artists painted landscapes on scrolls.

readings.section: CKVA Day 26: Pottery - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Sculpt a vase or bowl from clay. Artwork: Ming Dynasty Vase. Supplies: air-dry porcelain clay (3-5 lb), sculpting tools, rolling pin, cup of water, washable work surface.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 26: Pottery (The Art of China)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Identify the key features of traditional Chinese porcelain.

readings.section: CKVA Day 27: Unit 4 Assessment - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Paint your clay pottery with traditional Chinese imagery. Supplies: your clay pot from last lesson, blue ceramic or acrylic paint, paintbrush, cup of water, paper towels.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 27: Unit 4 Assessment (The Art of China)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Show understanding of the art of China.

readings.section: CKVA Day 28: Introduction to Art and Architecture of a New Nation - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Read and answer questions about early American portraits. Artwork: Paul Revere (John Singleton Copley).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 28: Introduction to Art and Architecture of a New Nation (Early United States)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Analyze the purpose of portraiture in colonial America.

ckva.lesson: Introduction to Art and Architecture of a New Nation

readings.section: CKVA Day 29: History Through an Artist's Lens - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Analyze the painting Washington Crossing the Delaware. Artwork: Washington Crossing the Delaware (Emanuel Leutze). Supplies: colored pencils.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 29: History Through an Artist's Lens (Early United States)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Analyze the purpose of history painting after the American Revolution.

readings.section: CKVA Day 30: Portrait of a Leader (day 1 of 2) - view the artwork online
readings.note: Analyze portraits of national heroes. Artwork: George Washington (Gilbert Stuart), Profile Bust of Benjamin Franklin (Patience Wright).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 30: Portrait of a Leader (day 1 of 2) (Early United States)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Analyze portraits of national heroes from the colonial and revolutionary periods.

readings.section: CKVA Day 31: Portrait of a Leader (day 2 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Draw a portrait of an inspiring early American leader. Supplies: drawing paper, pencil and eraser, colored pencils.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 31: Portrait of a Leader (day 2 of 2) (Early United States)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Analyze portraits of national heroes from the colonial and revolutionary periods.

readings.section: CKVA Day 32: Architecture to Represent Us - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Design your own neoclassical building after learning about Monticello. Artwork: Monticello (Thomas Jefferson). Supplies: sketch paper, drawing paper, pencil and eraser, colored pencils.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 32: Architecture to Represent Us (Early United States)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Recognize the features of American neoclassical architecture.

readings.section: CKVA Day 33: Unit 5 Assessment - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Reflect on architectural designs and review Unit 5. Supplies: pencil.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 33: Unit 5 Assessment (Early United States)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Show understanding of early American art and architecture.

readings.section: CKVA Day 34: Culminating Activity: A Year in Review (day 1 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Make a year-in-review booklet about the art you studied. Artwork: Madonna and Child on a Curved Throne, Illumination of the Qur'an, Portrait Head of an Ife King, Washington Crossing the Delaware. Supplies: blank booklet (folded paper), markers or colored pencils, pencil and eraser.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 34: Culminating Activity: A Year in Review (day 1 of 2) (Year in Review)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Summarize the features and purposes of the art studied this year.

ckva.lesson: Culminating Activity: A Year in Review

readings.section: CKVA Day 35: Culminating Activity: Gallery Show (day 2 of 2) - view the artwork online
readings.note: Set up a gallery of your artwork from the year and present it to the family. Supplies: your artwork from the year.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 35: Culminating Activity: Gallery Show (day 2 of 2) (Year in Review)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Present and explain your own artwork to an audience.

readings.section: CKVA Day 1: What Is Expressionism? - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Explore expressionist art and create an expressionist sketch. Artwork: The Scream (Edvard Munch). Supplies: heavy paper, pencil, kneaded and vinyl erasers, oil pastels.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 1: What Is Expressionism? (Expressionism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn the characteristics of the expressionist movement.

readings.section: CKVA Day 2: Fauvism (day 1 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Explore fauvism and begin a fauvist painting. Artwork: The Dessert: Harmony in Red (Henri Matisse). Supplies: heavy paper, pencil and erasers, tempera or acrylic paints, brush, palette, cup of water.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 2: Fauvism (day 1 of 2) (Expressionism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn the characteristics of fauvism.

readings.section: CKVA Day 3: Fauvism (day 2 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Compare impressionist and fauvist art and finish your fauvist painting. Supplies: your painting from Day 1, charcoal pencil, paints, brush, palette, water.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 3: Fauvism (day 2 of 2) (Expressionism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn the characteristics of fauvism.

readings.section: CKVA Day 4: Unit 1 Assessment - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Review Unit 1 and analyze another expressionist work (Indian Church). Artwork: Indian Church (Emily Carr).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 4: Unit 1 Assessment (Expressionism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Show understanding of expressionism and fauvism.

readings.section: CKVA Day 5: What Is Cubism? - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Learn the features of cubism and examine key works. Artwork: Le verre sur la table (Georges Braque).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 5: What Is Cubism? (Cubism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn the features of cubism.

readings.section: CKVA Day 6: Depicting a Scene (day 1 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Study Picasso's Guernica and draw a realistic scene in colored pencil. Artwork: Guernica (Pablo Picasso). Supplies: drawing paper, pencil, colored pencils.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 6: Depicting a Scene (day 1 of 2) (Cubism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Explore Guernica and create a cubist work.

readings.section: CKVA Day 7: Depicting a Scene (day 2 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Re-create your realistic scene in a cubist style. Supplies: drawing paper, scrap paper (4 sheets), erasers, scissors, glue.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 7: Depicting a Scene (day 2 of 2) (Cubism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Explore Guernica and create a cubist work.

readings.section: CKVA Day 8: Unit 2 Assessment - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Review Unit 2 and analyze Nude Descending a Staircase (No. 2). Artwork: Le verre sur la table, Guernica.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 8: Unit 2 Assessment (Cubism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Show understanding of cubism.

readings.section: CKVA Day 9: What Is Surrealism? - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Learn the features of surrealism and draw like a surrealist. Artwork: The Persistence of Memory (Salvador Dali). Supplies: drawing paper, pencil and vinyl eraser, colored pencils.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 9: What Is Surrealism? (Surrealism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn the features of surrealism.

readings.section: CKVA Day 10: Portraits - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Study surrealist portraits and make your own surrealist portrait. Artwork: Creation of the Birds (Remedios Varo), Self-Portrait (Leonora Carrington). Supplies: heavy paper, pencil and eraser, colored pencils, watercolors (optional).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 10: Portraits (Surrealism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn surrealist self-portraiture.

readings.section: CKVA Day 11: Max Ernst and Surrealist Techniques (day 1 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Explore Max Ernst's techniques and start a surrealist collage. Artwork: The Forest (Max Ernst). Supplies: heavy drawing paper, newspapers and magazines, construction paper, scissors.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 11: Max Ernst and Surrealist Techniques (day 1 of 2) (Surrealism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn Max Ernst's techniques (collage, frottage, grattage).

readings.section: CKVA Day 12: Max Ernst and Surrealist Techniques (day 2 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Finish your surrealist collage. Supplies: your collage from Day 1, glue.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 12: Max Ernst and Surrealist Techniques (day 2 of 2) (Surrealism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn Max Ernst's techniques (collage, frottage, grattage).

readings.section: CKVA Day 13: Unit 3 Assessment - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Present your collage and explain the surrealist techniques you used.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 13: Unit 3 Assessment (Surrealism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Show understanding of surrealism.

readings.section: CKVA Day 14: What Is Abstract Expressionism? - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Explore the features of abstract expressionism and analyze a Pollock painting. Artwork: Number 28, 1950 (Jackson Pollock).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 14: What Is Abstract Expressionism? (Abstract Expressionism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn the features of abstract expressionism.

readings.section: CKVA Day 15: Drip Painting - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Make a drip painting in the style of Jackson Pollock. Supplies: large heavy craft paper (24 in+), acrylic paints, brushes, spoons, squeeze bottles, newspaper or drop cloth (work outside if possible).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 15: Drip Painting (Abstract Expressionism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn the technique of drip painting.

readings.section: CKVA Day 16: A Study in Texture - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Explore texture and create a thickly painted textured work. Artwork: Night Light (Lee Krasner). Supplies: small canvas or heavy paper, acrylic paints, brush, palette knife (optional).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 16: A Study in Texture (Abstract Expressionism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn how abstract expressionists used texture.

readings.section: CKVA Day 17: A Study in Color - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Explore color fields and create an abstract color painting. Artwork: No. 9 (Mark Rothko), John F. Kennedy (Elaine de Kooning). Supplies: heavy paper, acrylic paints, brushes.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 17: A Study in Color (Abstract Expressionism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn how abstract expressionists used color.

readings.section: CKVA Day 18: Unit 4 Assessment - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Create an abstract work using the techniques from Unit 4. Supplies: heavy paper or small canvas, acrylic paints, brushes.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 18: Unit 4 Assessment (Abstract Expressionism)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Show understanding of abstract expressionism.

readings.section: CKVA Day 19: What Is Abstraction? - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Explore abstraction through Mondrian and Kandinsky. Artwork: Broadway Boogie Woogie (Piet Mondrian), Points (Wassily Kandinsky).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 19: What Is Abstraction? (Abstraction)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn the characteristics of abstraction.

readings.section: CKVA Day 20: Create Abstract Style (day 1 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Paint an abstract work in the style of Mondrian or Kandinsky. Supplies: heavy paper, pencil, markers, watercolors and brush.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 20: Create Abstract Style (day 1 of 2) (Abstraction)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Create two scenes in the abstract style.

readings.section: CKVA Day 21: Create Abstract Style (day 2 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Paint a second abstract work with different materials. Supplies: heavy paper, pencil, acrylic paints and brush.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 21: Create Abstract Style (day 2 of 2) (Abstraction)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Create two scenes in the abstract style.

readings.section: CKVA Day 22: Abstract Portraiture (day 1 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Study abstract portraits by Klee and Lois Mailou Jones. Artwork: Senecio (Paul Klee), Les fetiches (Lois Mailou Jones).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 22: Abstract Portraiture (day 1 of 2) (Abstraction)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn about abstract portraiture.

readings.section: CKVA Day 23: Abstract Portraiture (day 2 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Create an abstract portrait and compare it with your surrealist portrait. Supplies: heavy paper, pencil, paints or markers.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 23: Abstract Portraiture (day 2 of 2) (Abstraction)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn about abstract portraiture.

readings.section: CKVA Day 24: Abstraction in Nature (day 1 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Explore abstraction in nature paintings (O'Keeffe and others).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 24: Abstraction in Nature (day 1 of 2) (Abstraction)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn about abstraction in nature.

readings.section: CKVA Day 25: Abstraction in Nature (day 2 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Create an abstract nature scene. Supplies: heavy paper, pencil, markers, watercolors and brush.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 25: Abstraction in Nature (day 2 of 2) (Abstraction)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn about abstraction in nature.

readings.section: CKVA Day 26: The Gutai Group (day 1 of 3) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Explore the Gutai Group's work and mission.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 26: The Gutai Group (day 1 of 3) (Abstraction)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn about the Gutai Group.

readings.section: CKVA Day 27: The Gutai Group (day 2 of 3) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Create artwork using Gutai principles. Supplies: large heavy craft paper, acrylic paints, sponges or found tools, newspaper or drop cloth.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 27: The Gutai Group (day 2 of 3) (Abstraction)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn about the Gutai Group.

readings.section: CKVA Day 28: The Gutai Group (day 3 of 3) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Hold a gallery walk and compare your work with the Gutai Group.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 28: The Gutai Group (day 3 of 3) (Abstraction)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn about the Gutai Group.

readings.section: CKVA Day 29: Unit 5 Assessment - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Compare and contrast art from Unit 5.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 29: Unit 5 Assessment (Abstraction)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Show understanding of abstraction.

readings.section: CKVA Day 30: What Is Organic Architecture? - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Learn the features of organic architecture through four famous buildings. Artwork: Tassel House (Victor Horta), Guaranty Building (Sullivan and Adler), Darwin Martin House (Frank Lloyd Wright), Casa Batllo (Antoni Gaudi).

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 30: What Is Organic Architecture? (Twentieth-Century Architecture)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Learn the characteristics of organic architecture.

readings.section: CKVA Day 31: Architectural Design (day 1 of 2) - Student Activity Book
readings.note: Design a building using organic architecture. Supplies: paper or 1-inch graph paper, pencil, ruler, eraser.

teacher_readings.section: CKVA Day 31: Architectural Design (day 1 of 2) (Twentieth-Century Architecture)
teacher_readings.note: Objective: Design and model a building using organic architecture.

readings.section: CKVA Day 32: Architectural Design (day 2 of 2) - Student Activity Book
